correctness.rationale: For fixed epsilon>0 and mu→infinity, on each right/left oval q_mu(s,v)=16v^4+(mu s^2-25)v^2-a(s)=0 yields exact quadratic root and uniform v_mu(s)=mu^-1/2 sqrt(a(s))/s[1+O(mu^-1)], s∈[3/4,1]. Area is 2∫v ds=pi/(8sqrt(mu))+O(mu^-3/2); max sqrt(mu)|v|→1. Chemical tangential velocity on h=0 retains xy epsilon, and sum of both signed transverse branch time elements gives T_sigma=J_sigma/(2epsilon sqrt(mu))+O(mu^-3/2) with J_++J_-=pi/2(1/3+1/sqrt165). Cofactor dot h=-xy h|grad h|^2 yields rho=exp(-I_mu/epsilon), I_mu=2∫(D+H^2/D)ds=49pi sqrt(mu)/256+O(mu^-1/2). Dividing by period produces the two epsilon-independent linear-in-mu contraction rates. Branch time densities converge under integrable a(s)^-1/2 envelope to the stated nonuniform axial occupation and two signed scaled-transverse graphs. Independent check: Constructed independent numerical quadratures from exact quartic root and branchwise time element at mu=100,1000,10000. Computed J+=0.183147394958, J-=0.462737708834, matching pi/2(1/3+1/sqrt165)=0.645885103789. At mu=10000 measured sqrt(mu)area≈0.393355 vs pi/8≈0.392699; I_mu/sqrt(mu)≈0.604173 vs 49pi/256≈0.601320; 2sqrt(mu)*periods approach the J constants. The asymptotic proof is based on uniform expansions, not numerical extrapolation.
